header.running_head: The Bond of Brotherhood Between the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar (RA)

blocks.text: A Few Couplets Composed by Hadhrat Sirmah bin Qais (RA) in this regard

Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed narrates from an old lady from the Ansaar that she used to see Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) frequently visit Hadhrat Sirma bin Qais (RA) to learn the following couplets (which mean):

"He stayed with the Quraysh for a few years more than ten
Advising people with the hope of meeting a suitable friend
Offering himself to the people coming for Hajj
Without seeing anyone to offer asylum nor anyone offering an invitation
When he came to us (Ansaar) and settled
He became happy and pleased in Tayba (Madinah)
He then had no fear of a distant tyrant oppressively taking something away
Nor any fear of people revolting
For him we spent most of our wealth
As well as our lives in battles and in comforting (the Muhaajireen)
We were enemies of all those who were his enemies
Even though they had been the best of our friends
(All this because) We were convinced that there is nothing (worthy of worship) but Allaah
And that the Book of Allaah is our guide" [^1]
The Bond of Brotherhood Between the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar (RA)
The Story of Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) and Hadhrat Sa'd bin Rabee (RA)

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) arrived in Madinah, Rasulullaah ﷺ established a bond of brotherhood between him and Hadhrat Sa'd bin Rabee Ansaari (RA). Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) said to Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA), "Dear brother! I am the wealthiest person in Madinah and you may have half of my wealth. I also have two wives. You may choose the one you like best and I shall divorce her." Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) replied, "May Allaah bless you in your family and wealth. Just show me the way to the marketplace." When Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) showed Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) where the marketplace was, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) started buying and selling until he had made a profit. He returned with some cheese and butter.
He continued like this for a while until one day he appeared with the colour of saffron on his clothes. "What is this all about?" asked Rasulullaah ﷺ. "I have married," he replied. "What dowry did you give your wife?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked further. Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) replied, "The weight of a date stone in gold."
